messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Pager: auth-service (vpc-auth) high error rate for tenant opalbridge in us-west-2. 5xx/401 spikes, latency above SLO. Runbook: <https://redwood-internal/runbooks/vpc-auth>

miguel: seeing the same in prod metrics. OpalBridge tenant specifically. auth-introspect 504 -> idp timeout, and a burst of 401s.

aisha: opalbridge confirmed they rotated client certs earlier this morning? @opalbridge-sre can you confirm what changed?

opalbridge-sre: we rotated our client certs at 09:02 PDT, rolled out to 60% of clients. No other changes on our side. We started seeing increased latencies ~09:12. We'll hold further rollouts.

sara: ok, tagging oncall. @miguel you're primary - can you triage? if this is cert mismatch, should be 401, but we're also seeing 504 to upstream idp.

miguel: onit. checking ingress logs for TLS handshakes + jwks fetch. quick grep:

```
2026-03-15T16:11:23Z auth-proxy[opalbridge] WARN jwks fetch 403 from idp.internal
2026-03-15T16:11:25Z auth-proxy[opalbridge] ERROR introspect timeout after 2.1s
2026-03-15T16:11:26Z auth-proxy[opalbridge] WARN clientcert handshake failed: unknown_ca
```

rick: hmm unknown_ca -> sounds like the client cert chain doesn't include the intermediate CA we expect. But jwks 403 is weird; idp should return 200. Could be key rotation + JWKS access control.

jenn: noticed a spike in eviction events on the dedicated pool for opalbridge (dedicated-pool-13). Could be auth hotloop causing repeated reconnects -> token cache thrash.

miguel: confirming: token KV cache is being invalidated because failures on introspect. That increases calls to idp -> we hit idp rate limits -> 403/429 -> chain reaction.

aisha: impact summary for customer-facing comms: opalbridge - login failures, failed calls that require bearer validation, and slow requests. Estimate: ~28% of requests failing with 401/502 and median latency +180ms for auth path. hitting their tenant SLA.

opalbridge-sre: we can temporarily revert client cert rollout to previous thumbprint if that helps. But we need guidance on server-side mitigations.

miguel: mitigation plan proposal:
- Step A: add short-circuit fallback for opalbridge on our auth-proxy: if introspect fails with 5xx/timeout, use cached token validation for 30s instead of immediate fail (temporary safe relax) -> reduces idp calls.
- Step B: throttle introspect retries and implement jitter to avoid thundering herd.
- Step C: add a JWKS fallback to previously cached JWKS and allow key lookup by kid even if remote fetch errors.
- Step D: coordinate cert rollback with opalbridge if client cert chain is broken.

sara: I like A+B+C, low-risk. Who can deploy the auth-proxy quick patch to dedicated-pool config? @jenn? we need a canary to opalbridge only.

jenn: I can push a config patch to auth-proxy routing for tenant opalbridge to enable fallback caching boolean: `opalbridge_auth_fallback=true`. Will run canary to 10% of nodes in pool first.

deploy-bot: deploy started: service=auth-proxy, env=prod, target=dedicated-pool-13(canary 10%), change=enable tenant fallback cache flag. CI checks passed.

miguel: rolling. monitoring logs and telemetry.

[~5m pass]

miguel: canary looks good so far — introspect call volume down ~60% for canary nodes, 401 rates dropped ~40% for affected hosts. No errors from canary stacks.

aisha: push to 100% if canary holds. Still need to coordinate JWKS fallback though; current code drops request if JWKS fetch 403.

jenn: pushing to 100% now.

deploy-bot: deploy completed: target=dedicated-pool-13(100%). All checks green.

miguel: auth error rate decreased cluster-wide to baseline-ish but still elevated due to idp rate-limit burst. JWKS errors remain intermittently 403.

rick: I dug into idp logs (we have access via opalbridge partnership). The idp returned 403 because of a missing client header used for auth when fetching tenant-specific JWKS after key rotation. Looks like our upstream service rotated the header validation. We need to use the new header or request opalbridge to adjust idp config.

opalbridge-sre: confirmed: idp started enforcing `X-Tenant-Key-Token` header on JWKS fetch after the cert rotation. We didn't know. Our side can add the header on client fetches but the vendor asked for a signed timestamp which we can't produce instantly.

miguel: two parallel tracks then: A) we keep the fallback caching patch in place to reduce pressure and B) we request opalbridge to either temporarily whitelist our auth-proxy client IPs for JWKS or provide the signed header token.

aisha: ops comms draft for customer-facing update:
"We identified increased auth failures for OpalBridge starting 09:12 PDT caused by client cert chain mismatch combined with enforced JWKS access controls at your IdP after your rotation. We have deployed a temporary fallback in our auth-proxy to reduce impact while working with you on rotation rollback or token-based JWKS access. Next update in 30m."

opalbridge-sre: will attempt to whitelist our IPs for JWKS fetch. ETA 20m. rolling back client certs now to previous thumbprint as well.

miguel: after rollback confirmation:

opalbridge-sre: rollback complete at 09:44 PDT. We stopped the cert rollout.

miguel: checking metrics: 401s dropped substantially after rollback and our fallback. idp 403s also reduced once whitelist applied.

jenn: there is still a small residual latency bump due to token cache warm-up. estimate full recovery in ~15-30m.

sara: who's owning postmortem? we need RCA covering: JWKS access control change not communicated, cert rollout without validating JWKS policy, our auth-proxy lacking JWKS fallback & header support.

miguel: I'll own the tech RCA (auth-proxy changes + JWKS fallback enhancement). @opalbridge-sre can you own change comms + your rollout process notes? I'll pair with you.

opalbridge-sre: yes, we'll provide timeline and change approval gaps.

aisha: followup actions and owners (short list):
- implement signed-header support for JWKS fetch and config toggle per-tenant (owner: miguel)
- add permanent safe-fallback caching with strict TTL and audit logging (owner: jenn)
- update runbook to check idp JWKS access policy before cert rotations for tenants using tenant-specific jwks (owner: sara)
- customer postmortem coordination (owner: aisha)

miguel: temporary mitigations remain in prod until we ship header support. I'll open PR and target hotfix in 24h.

sara: good. Incident severity -> Sev2 (customer-impacting, mitigated). I'll update incident channel + page rotation.

incident-bot: Incident updated: sev=2, status=mitigated. Incident link: <https://redwood-incidents/3929001111>

aisha: sending the 30m update to opalbridge now.

opalbridge-sre: thanks team. appreciate the quick mitigation and the rollback assist.

miguel: logging note: we should also add a metric for jwks_403_by_tenant to catch this earlier.

jenn: created ticket INF-5632: jwks header & fallback + metric. PR link: <https://git.internal/p/INF-5632>

sara: closing timeline: first alert 3929001111 (09:15), canary patch 09:27, rollback 09:44, mitigated 09:52. Will leave channel open for next 2 hours for any regressions.

opalbridge-sre: we'll run additional validation on our next cert rollout and coordinate with you. thanks.

miguel: thumbs. :thumbsup:
